chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa narrated to me from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from Fadala from Sayf b. 'Umayra from 'Ubaydullah b. 'Abdullah from one who heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said when the month of Ramadan approached, three days before the end of Sha'ban, he said to Bilal: Call the people. So the people gathered, then he climbed the pulpit, praised Allah and commended Him, then said: O people! Indeed this month has approached you, and it is the Master of Months. In it there is a night that is better than a thousand months. In it the gates of Hell are locked and the gates of Paradise are opened. Whoever comes unto it yet is not forgiven, Allah cuts him off. Whoever has his parents yet is not forgiven, Allah cuts him off. Whoever has me mentioned in his midst yet does not send blessings on me and is not forgiven, Allah cuts him off.

key_terms.سيد الشهور: Master of Months, the highest-ranking month
key_terms.فأبعده الله: may Allah cut him off/distance him
key_terms.ليلة خير من ألف شهر: a night better than a thousand months (Laylat al-Qadr)

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about the virtues of Ramadan in his sermon before the month began?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition, narrated through Imam al-Baqir (AS), records the Prophet Muhammad's (S) sermon delivered three days before Ramadan began during the month of Sha'ban. The Prophet ordered Bilal to gather the people, then ascended the pulpit to announce Ramadan's virtues: it is the Master of Months, contains a night better than a thousand months (Laylat al-Qadr), and its gates of Hell close while Paradise opens. He then pronounced three supplications of distancing (ab'adahu Allah) for those who fail to gain forgiveness through: the month itself, serving their parents, and sending blessings upon the Prophet when he is mentioned.
